Kai: Heads up — I hit a perf regression on Mistral-8x7B when running sliding-window with RoPE scale > 1.0. Latency started jittering and the kernel selector flips between kv_gemm and kv_slice within the same streaming request.

Maria: How did you reproduce this?

Kai: Single-stream streaming client, window=2048, prefix cached (~1024). Requests around 600 tokens. With rope_scale=1.0 p50 ~ 40-45ms/token. With rope_scale=1.2 p50 jumps to ~55-60ms/token and tails spike. Observed kernel-selector switching mid-sequence.

perf-bot: kernel-selection trace: [1773051236] model=mistral-8x7b scale=1.2 seq=600 -> chosen=kv_slice
perf-bot: kernel-selection trace: [1773051238] model=mistral-8x7b scale=1.2 seq=680 -> chosen=kv_gemm

Owen: Do we have profiler samples around the decision points?

Kai: Yes — sampled selector inputs and lightweight nvprof. Snippet below:
```
1773051239: selector::estimate -> gemm=12.3ms slice=9.6ms
1773051240: selector::estimate -> gemm=26.0ms slice=25.7ms
1773051240: launch(gemm)
1773051242: launch(slice)
```

Sasha: Strange. Why would gemm's estimate jump so much mid-run? Could RoPE interpolation be shifting logical->physical cache indices so tile counts change?

Maria: That's my hunch. The RoPE rescaling code uses an interpolation path that does some rounding of position indices. If that rounding changes which 128-sized tile a request maps into, our cost model (which assumes tile-aligned memory patterns) can flip choice when kv_cache_len crosses a multiple-of-tile boundary.

Owen: Can we dump the selector inputs for the two decision points? I want seq_prefix/current, rope_scale, kv_dim, heads, kv_cache_len, and any cache-hit metrics.

Kai: Dumped inputs:
[case A] seq_prefix=1024 seq_curr=600 rope_scale=1.2 kv_dim=64 heads=16 kv_cache_len=1624
[case B] seq_prefix=1024 seq_curr=680 rope_scale=1.2 kv_dim=64 heads=16 kv_cache_len=1704
Selector predicted gemm faster for A and slice faster for B. The delta lines up with crossing a 128-tile boundary (~1664/1792).

Sasha: That explains the jitter. Two quick mitigations: 1) have the selector compute tiles = ceil(kv_cache_len / TILE_SZ) instead of floor; 2) add a small hysteresis so the selector needs a >5% win to switch kernels.

Maria: Another angle: make the RoPE interpolation deterministic w.r.t. rounding so logical positions map consistently to cache indices. Also add a unit test sweep for rope_scale in 1.1..1.3 to catch boundary flips.

Owen: Proposed patch in selector.cpp: replace floor division with ceil:
```
// before
tiles = kv_cache_len / TILE_SZ;
// after
tiles = (kv_cache_len + TILE_SZ - 1) / TILE_SZ;
// and multiply memcpy estimate by 1.05 as a small buffer against tiny noise
```
Add a 1.05 multiplier to memcpy cost and require ~5% advantage to flip.

Kai: I implemented a local patch (ceil-tiling + 1.05 memcpy factor) and added a tiny perf harness test. Ran 200 iterations: p50 returned to ~44ms/token, tails reduced, and no in-request kernel flips observed. Numerical diff on a synthetic attention check was small (L2 ~0.02) — within interpolation tolerances.

perf-bot: scheduled nightly sweep job for mistral-8x7b: rope_scale=1.0..1.3 with sliding-window workloads. Report due by 08:00 UTC tomorrow. :white_check_mark:

Owen: LGTM. Follow-ups: merge selector change + test, add CI perf regression check for the rope_scale sweep, and add logging whenever a kernel switch happens mid-request so future debugging has clearer traces.

Sasha: I'll ping infra to run a Dedicated-cluster smoke test with long sliding-window clients (to catch any Dedicated-only artifacts).

Kai: Opening PR with patch, test, and profiler snippets in the PR description. Marking thread status -> in-progress.
